f.title: Include the minimum elements in the pharmacovigilance system
f.statement: A good pharmacovigilance system should contain at least: standard operating procedures (SOPs), training and competence, IT systems, a documentation system, and continuous improvement based on audits, inspections and updates to GVP.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
In general, a Good Pharmacovigilance system should contain at least
the following elements: standard operating procedures (SOPs), training and competence, IT Systems,
documentation system and continuous improvement based on audits, inspections, and updates to
GVP.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Reflect PV responsibilities and oversight provisions in contracts with service providers
f.statement: Contracts and agreements with all relevant parties should appropriately reflect responsibilities and activities in the fulfilment of pharmacovigilance and cover, among others: pre-selection audits, gap analysis and capacity planning; record/data ownership and MAH access to source data and the safety database; records management (format, location, timely provision) and retention periods; transition terms (especially data transfers) and termination rules; business continuity; proportionate oversight tools (audit, KPIs, deviations); QPPV and national competent authority access to data and documentation; sharing of inspection and audit outcomes and CAPA implementation; workload metrics and resource/training allocation; and dispute resolution. Organisations performing PV activities for the MAH may themselves be inspected.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Contracts and agreements with all relevant parties appropriately reflect
                 responsibilities and activities in the fulfilment of pharmacovigilance, and adhere to
                 the following points but not limited to:
rows.review_note: Review: stated as an element of the routine inspection scope; level Recommended since phrased as an inspection expectation. Double-check: ok.

f.title: Prepare for GVP inspections and keep inspection-ready at all times
f.statement: The MAH shall prepare for the GVP inspection and is advised to conduct self-audits and confirm readiness at all times and before the planned inspection.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
The MAH shall also have a responsibility to prepare for the GVP inspection. The MAH is advised to
conduct self-audits and confirm readiness at all times and before the planned GVP inspection.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Compile and make available inspection documents and brief staff
f.statement: The MAH shall compile and readily make available the required documents and brief its staff about the inspection. Documents EFDA may request before an inspection (notified about 14 calendar days ahead) include the PSMF reflecting the Ethiopian PV system, the list of important SOPs (Annex IV), PV meeting minutes, individual adverse reaction case files, recent PSURs/PBRERs, CAPA records, country-specific RMPs and line listings of adverse reaction reports.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
In
addition, the MAH shall compile and readily avail required documents as well as conduct briefing to
their staff regarding the inspection.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Facilitate the inspection and provide all requested information
f.statement: During a pharmacovigilance inspection, the MAH must take the necessary measures to facilitate the inspection and is required to provide all requested information and documentation relevant to the inspection scope.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
During a pharmacovigilance inspection, the MAH must take necessary measures to facilitate the
inspection process and ensure compliance with Good Vigilance Practice (GVP) guidelines. They are
required to provide all requested information and documentation relevant to the inspection scope.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: File any complaint on inspection findings within 10 working days
f.statement: After receiving the official inspection report, the MAH may file a complaint on the findings within 10 working days; otherwise the report is considered accepted by the MAH.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.deadline: 10 working days from receipt of the official inspection report
rows.quote:
After receiving the official inspection report, if the MAH does not file any complaint
on the findings of the inspection within 10 working days, the report will be considered as accepted
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

deadline_rule.clock_start: After receiving the official inspection report

f.title: Submit a CAPA plan within 20 working days of the inspection report
f.statement: The MAH shall provide an appropriate corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plan within 20 working days (using the CAPA plan template in Annex 2).
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.deadline: 20 working days (after receiving the official inspection report)
rows.quote:
The MAH shall provide an appropriate corrective and preventive action plan (CAPA)
within 20 working days.
rows.review_note: Review: clock start inferred from the preceding sentence on receipt of the report. Double-check: ok, kept at 88.

deadline_rule.clock_start: After receiving the official inspection report
deadline_rule.applies_to: CAPA plan responding to GVP inspection findings

f.title: Take immediate action on critical or major findings when required
f.statement: In certain circumstances the MAH may be required to take immediate action to address critical or major findings, for the protection of public health and safety.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
In certain circumstances, the MAH may be required to take immediate
action to address critical or major findings, for the protection of public health and safety.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Know the classification of inspection findings (critical, major, minor)
f.statement: Findings are classified as critical (adversely affects patients, poses a potential public-health risk or is a serious violation, e.g. fraud, falsification of data, failure to report serious unexpected adverse reactions within regulatory timelines), major (could potentially adversely affect patients or is a violation, e.g. inconsistently followed SOPs, missing documentation of internal audits, incomplete PV training records) or minor (not expected to adversely affect patients).
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
Critical: a deficiency in pharmacovigilance systems, practices or processes that adversely
          affects the rights, safety or well-being of patients or that poses a potential risk to public health
          or that represents a serious violation of applicable EFDA legislation and guidelines.
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it drives CAPA priority; level Recommended (definition). Double-check: ok.

f.title: Complete the CAPA plan under EFDA follow-up
f.statement: When non-compliance is identified during an inspection, follow-up is required until the CAPA plan is completed; follow-up may include review of the CAPA plan and periodic progress reports, re-inspection, requests to submit previously unsubmitted data or variations, requests for safety communications, meetings with the MAH, and product-related actions.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
When non-compliance with pharmacovigilance obligations is identified during an inspection, follow-
up will be required until a corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plan is completed.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Set up a PV system and appoint a QPPV residing in Ethiopia
f.statement: Every marketing authorisation holder should set up a robust pharmacovigilance system for its medicinal products and appoint a qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance who resides in Ethiopia.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Pharmacovigilance Directive No.932/2022 states that every Marketing Authorization Holder should
have responsibilities to set-up robust pharmacovigilance systems for their medicinal products and to
appoint a qualified person responsible for Pharmacovigilance who resides in Ethiopia.
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory because the guideline restates a duty of Directive 932/2022 although it says "should". Double-check: ok.

f.title: Assign a QPPV and backup QPPV before importing and distributing products
f.statement: The MAH should assign a QPPV and an appropriate backup QPPV before importation and distribution of its product in the Ethiopian market.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.deadline: Before importation and distribution of the product in Ethiopia
rows.quote:
Assign QPPV and appropriate backup QPPV before importation and distribution of its product in the
       Ethiopian market.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Ensure the QPPV is trained, has sufficient authority and adequate resources
f.statement: The MAH should provide or ensure comprehensive PV training for the QPPV, ensure the QPPV has sufficient authority to implement all PV activities, and ensure appropriate processes, resources and communication mechanisms are in place for the QPPV's responsibilities.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Provide and/or ensure that the QPPV has received comprehensive training in
       Pharmacovigilance.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Notify EFDA of QPPV absence and substitution plan within 14 calendar days
f.statement: The MAH should notify the Authority of the absence of the QPPV and the substitution plan not later than 14 calendar days after the position becomes vacant.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.deadline: Not later than 14 calendar days after the position becomes vacant
rows.quote:
Notify the Authority of the absence of the QPPV and substitution plan not later than 14
       calendar days after the position becomes vacant.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Notification of QPPV vacancy and substitution plan

f.title: Sign a contract with the QPPV using the EFDA template
f.statement: The MAH should have a signed contract agreement with the QPPV, following the template in Annex V (which empowers the local QPPV to act as EFDA contact, maintain the ADR collection and forwarding system, be available during inspections and prepare/submit safety documents).
f.clause: 4.1 Responsibilities of the MAH; Annex V
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: Have a signed contract agreement with the QPPV.
rows.location: 4.1 Responsibilities of the MAH; Annex V
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit QPPV information to EFDA on assignment
f.statement: On assignment of the QPPV, the MAH should submit to the Authority: the CV with proof of qualifications and credentials; contact details (name, telephone, fax, e-mail, postal and official working address); a description of the QPPV's roles and responsibilities; back-up arrangements for the QPPV's absence; a list of tasks delegated by the QPPV and to whom; and the QPPV-MAH contract agreement as per Annex V.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The following QPPV related information should be submitted to the Authority during the
       assignment of QPPV.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have back-up procedures and a qualified backup QPPV
f.statement: The MAH should have back-up procedures for the absence of the QPPV and ensure that the backup QPPV meets the basic requirements: a healthcare professional with at least a bachelor's degree in health sciences who has received appropriate PV training.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The MAH should have back-up procedures in the case of absence of the QPPV and ensure
        that the backup QPPV shall meet the basic requirements
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Appoint a QPPV with health-science degree and two years of PV experience
f.statement: The QPPV should be a healthcare professional with at least a bachelor's degree in health sciences and at least two years of experience in pharmacovigilance-related activities; EFDA highly recommends pharmacists or medical doctors with appropriate PV training.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The person designated as QPPV should be a healthcare professional with a minimum of a
        bachelor’s degree in health sciences and at least two years of experience in
        pharmacovigilance-related activities.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV receives formal PV training from an acceptable institution
f.statement: The QPPV should receive formal training in pharmacovigilance from training institutions acceptable to the Authority.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The QPPV should receive formal training in pharmacovigilance from training institutions
        acceptable by the authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV is proficient in English and a national language of Ethiopia
f.statement: The assigned QPPV should be proficient in English and understand at least one of the national languages of Ethiopia.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The assigned QPPV should be proficient in English and understand at least one of the
        national languages of Ethiopia.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV acts as single point of contact for EFDA
f.statement: The QPPV should act as the single point of contact for the Authority on all matters relating to pharmacovigilance and safety of marketed products, including pharmacovigilance inspections.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Act as a single point of contact for the authority on all matters relating to pharmacovigilance
        and safety of marketed products including pharmacovigilance inspections.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV is a full-time MAH employee reachable 24/7
f.statement: The QPPV should be a full-time employee representing the MAH and should be reachable 24/7. Where a QPPV works as a full-time employee in more than one company, the Authority will take administrative action.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
The QPPV should be a full-time employee representing the MAH and should be reachable
        24/7.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV maintains a system to collect, process and forward all suspected AEs
f.statement: The QPPV should establish and maintain a system ensuring that information about all suspected adverse events reported to the MAH by any means is collected, collated, processed, evaluated and forwarded to the Authority within the timelines stipulated by EFDA.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Within the timelines stipulated by EFDA
rows.quote:
Establish and maintain a system that ensures information about all suspected adverse events,
        which are reported to the marketing authorization holder by any means, are collected,
        collated, processed, evaluated, and forwarded to the authority in line with the timelines
        stipulated by EFDA.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV prepares PSURs/PBRERs, study reports, safety variations and ongoing evaluations
f.statement: The QPPV should prepare for submission to the Authority: PSURs/PBRERs; company-sponsored pre- and post-registration study reports related to PV; risk management plans; safety variations; and ongoing pharmacovigilance evaluation during the post-registration period.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: Prepare the following documents for submission to the authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Accompany every RMP with a declaration signed by the QPPV
f.statement: All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration signed by the QPPV stating that the QPPV has read the RMP and will ensure implementation of all activities outlined in it.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Risk Management Plans - All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration
               to be signed by the QPPV. The declaration should indicate that the QPPV has read
               the RMP and will ensure implementation of all activities outlined in the RMP.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Review local and international literature and submit published suspected AEs
f.statement: The QPPV should regularly review both local and international journals and submit to the Authority published suspected adverse events occurring in and outside Ethiopia related to the company's products.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Review both local and international journals regularly, submit to the Authority in case of
       published suspected AEs which occur in and outside Ethiopia related to their medical
       products.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Provide EFDA requests for benefit-risk information promptly and fully
f.statement: The QPPV should ensure that any request from the Authority for additional information necessary for evaluating the benefit-risk ratio of a marketed product is answered promptly and fully.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Ensure that any request from the authority for additional information deemed necessary for
       the evaluation of the risk-benefit ratio of a marketed product is provided to the authority
       promptly and fully.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Oversee product safety profiles and emerging safety concerns
f.statement: The QPPV should oversee the safety profiles of the company's marketed products and any emerging safety concerns.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Oversee the safety profiles of the company’s marketed products and any emerging safety
       concerns.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Ensure PV submissions meet Directive 932/2022 requirements and timelines
f.statement: The QPPV should ensure submission of pharmacovigilance documents in compliance with regulatory requirements and timelines in the national Pharmacovigilance Directive 932/2022, and ensure the quality of data submitted to the Authority.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote:
Ensure the submission of Pharmacovigilance related documents in compliance with
       Regulatory requirements and timelines as indicated on the national Pharmacovigilance
       Directive 932/2022.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Document and archive PV documents properly
f.statement: The QPPV should ensure proper documentation and archiving of pharmacovigilance-related documents.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: Ensure the proper documentation and archival of Pharmacovigilance related documents.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV trains staff, takes CPD and leads PV self-audits
f.statement: The QPPV should provide pharmacovigilance training to staff, take continuous professional development training on safety issues, and lead and coordinate pharmacovigilance self-audits.
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: Provide Pharmacovigilance training to staff.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Include the minimum EFDA content in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF shall contain at minimum: cover letter (MAH and QPPV details, list of PSMFs, version and effective date); quality management system (SOPs, training records, audit schedules and audits); organisational structure and outsourcing/contracts; QPPV roles, CVs and contacts; PV processes (ICSRs, signals, RMPs, PSURs/PBRERs); sources of safety data; databases and IT systems (description, data integrity and backup); PV performance metrics; audit and inspection reports; training plan and business continuity plan; and annexes (SOP list, organisational chart, safety data flow diagram, logbook of changes, process workflows, document control, product and MAH lists, database validation documentation).
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: Minimum information that the Pharmacovigilance system master file (PSMF) shall contains
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Maintain the important PV SOPs listed by EFDA
f.statement: The MAH should have, and be able to list for inspection, important SOPs covering: ICSR processing; CAPA; safety communications; internal audit; literature searches; management of PV inspections; risk management systems and monitoring of risk-minimisation outcomes; implementation of safety variations; review and submission of regulatory documents (PSURs/PBRERs, RMPs); signal generation; training; and PSMF maintenance.
f.clause: 3.1 Pre-inspection activities; Annex 4: List of SOPs
f.applicability: MAHs placing medicinal products for human use on the Ethiopian market

rows.quote: List of Important SOPs as per Annex IV
rows.location: 3.1 Pre-inspection activities; Annex 4: List of SOPs
rows.review_note: Review: no modal; derived from the list of documents EFDA may request. Double-check: Recommended, kept below 90.
